Paddock.body:
## macOS download for 1.7

Version 1.7.2 brings the macOS package back. For Windows and Linux it behaves the same as 1.7.1; updating is harmless but not needed.

- **macOS:** the checks that every macOS package must pass run on a newer version of the database engine. That version exposed a weakness in how the racing-history pages (session results, lap pages, a car's history, results received from Timing) read their lists of participants and lanes. Those queries are corrected, so they work on both the current and the newer engine. The published 1.7.0 and 1.7.1 apps use the current engine and were not affected.
- **Parts lists:** the NSR, ScaleAuto and Slot.it lists are now attached to every release automatically.

## New in 1.7

- **Automatic backups:** Paddock makes complete backups on a schedule (Settings > Database). It is on by default: weekly, keeping the newest 5. Choose daily, weekly or monthly, another folder, or use "Back up now".
- **Move the shared library:** move the library to another folder on this computer from Settings > Database. Timing follows it at its next start.
- **Search everything:** press Ctrl+K, `/` or the Search button to search cars, parts, workshop jobs, manuals, pages and commands.
- **Keyboard shortcuts:** Ctrl+N, Ctrl+F, Ctrl+`,` and Alt+1–9; press `?` for the list.
- **Update notice:** Paddock shows when a newer release is available, with a Download button. It only asks GitHub for the latest version number, and can be switched off in Settings > Database > Updates.
- **Lap-based maintenance reminders:** Record work accepts "after this many laps", counted from Timing races and manual track tests.
- **Collection value chart:** the Overview shows current value and spending per purchase year, per currency.
- **Faster everyday use:** the Cars list, Showroom, Settings, Shopping List, Find a Part and search respond several times faster on large collections.
- **Spreadsheet import:** step 2 lists what blocks "Choose cars", with a button to fix each problem.
- **Fixed:** a crash after adding a part from the Parts page, and a double scrollbar in the search box.

## Downloads

- **Windows installer:** `SlotForgePaddock-1.7.2-Setup.exe` updates the installed application while keeping its existing collection and settings.
- **Windows portable:** `SlotForgePaddock-1.7.2-Portable.exe` runs without installation.
- **Source:** `SlotForgePaddock-1.7.2-source.zip` is the tagged source: the app, build files and tests.
- **Linux:** native x64 and ARM64 packages, each as AppImage and .deb.
- **macOS:** `SlotForgePaddock-1.7.2-mac-universal.dmg` (or the .zip) for Intel and Apple Silicon. The app is not signed with an Apple developer certificate, so macOS asks for approval the first time; see the [macOS notes](https://github.com/theDutchmanJames/SlotForgePaddock/blob/main/docs/BUILDING.md).
- **Parts lists (optional):** the NSR, ScaleAuto and Slot.it lists are attached to this release, supplied separately from the app. [What they contain and how to import them](https://github.com/theDutchmanJames/SlotForgePaddock/blob/main/parts-lists/README.md).

## Validation

1,865 automated tests on Windows: 1,856 passed, zero failures, nine optional tests skipped. The same suite passed on Linux x64, Linux ARM64 and macOS before their packages were attached. Syntax checks passed for 296 JavaScript files. The full interface smoke test passed all 230 checks. Every application file inside the Windows package was compared with the tagged source and matches.

Timing.body:
## SlotForge Timing 2.3.0

Easier race nights, much faster screens with a large history, and DS races that reach the shared library. No database conversion or schema change.

**Race night**
- Setup guide for a fresh install: track, drivers, cars, timing hardware, a sensor test and a 3-lap test race. Every step can be skipped.
- Test sensors on Home: each lane lights up when its sensor sees a car.
- DS Electronics: choose whether laps driven during a pause are ignored or added when the race resumes.
- Virtual DS box and virtual Trackmate for trying Timing without hardware.
- USB timing hardware is detected when plugged in: a known device reconnects, a new one is offered on Home.
- Pair a phone with the Race Director by QR code. On a phone the race controls stay at the top.

**Data**
- Automatic backups, daily or weekly, keeping the newest few.
- Share results as a web page, a CSV file or a text for a club chat.
- Driver progress on each driver's card: best and average lap and consistency per track and month.
- Records of races that the shared library has not accepted yet still count, marked as such.

**Ease of use**
- Problems show as chips on Home that open the page where they are fixed.
- Timing's own dialogs replace the Windows pop-ups; laps keep counting while a question is open.
- Notification of a newer release on GitHub (notify only) and Save diagnostics for bug reports.
- Search across App Settings, and hide the Race Setup systems your club never uses.
- Every built-in theme meets WCAG AA contrast for text; visible keyboard focus everywhere; reduced motion when Windows asks for it.

**Faster** (measured with 300 races and 62 cars, shared library on)
- Home 3.8 s → 0.3 s, Results and Records 10.4 s → about 1 s, start 4.8 s → 2.3 s.
- Updated shared-library engine from Paddock with faster library requests.

**Fixed**
- Races that never reached the shared library: keyboard-timed races (lap-time rounding) and DS-timed races (measured lap times against serial arrival moments).
- DS pause and resume messages, crossings during a pause that disappeared silently, and lag from DS signal polling.
- Connected timing hardware that was not "in use" counted no laps without saying so: now warned about on the hardware page, at Start race and on the race screen.
- Timing follows the shared library when Paddock moves it to another folder, without a restart.
- Fixes from a full review: the race page after finalizing, a hardened local-network server, storage, engine and screen issues.

### Downloads

- **Windows Portable.exe:** run without installing; includes the unpacking splash.
- **Windows Setup.exe:** install Timing for regular use.
- **macOS DMG / ZIP:** universal build for Intel and Apple Silicon.
- **Linux AppImage / Debian package:** choose the format for your distribution.

`SHA256SUMS.txt` covers the downloads. Windows packages are unsigned; the macOS app is ad-hoc signed, not Apple notarized.

Circuit.body:
A small update: Live preview now shows a car on every lane.

## What's new

- **One car per lane:** Live preview drives a car on every lane of the layout, up to 8, instead of only the first two. A 4-lane table now shows 4 cars. Lane 1 stays red and lane 2 blue; lanes 3–8 are green, yellow, orange, purple, teal and pink.

## Verification

57 unit test files passed on Windows, macOS and Linux, and 29 interface tests clicking through the real app passed on Windows and macOS. A new interface test opens a 2-lane and a 4-lane layout and checks that each lane has its own car and colour.

## Install or update

| System | Installer | Portable app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | `SlotForgeCircuit-0.4.1-Setup-x64.exe` | `SlotForgeCircuit-0.4.1-Portable-x64.exe` |
| macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) | `SlotForgeCircuit-0.4.1-mac-universal.dmg` | `SlotForgeCircuit-0.4.1-mac-universal.zip` |
| Linux (x64) | `SlotForgeCircuit-0.4.1-linux-amd64.deb` | `SlotForgeCircuit-0.4.1-linux-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux (ARM) | `SlotForgeCircuit-0.4.1-linux-arm64.deb` | `SlotForgeCircuit-0.4.1-linux-arm64.AppImage` |

Circuit is not code-signed: on Windows choose **More info → Run anyway**, or right-click the downloaded file → **Properties** → **Unblock**; on macOS right-click the app and choose **Open** the first time; on Linux mark the AppImage as executable (`chmod +x`). The SHA256SUMS files list each download's checksum.

Install over 0.4.0 as before: your saved tracks and packs stay where they are. Storage formats and the SlotForge Timing integration are unchanged.

Telemetry.body:
**SlotForge Telemetry 0.14.0 brings the app to the track: a Track day page for the change → drive → compare loop, a Garage for your cars and tracks, automatic backups, and a Windows installer.**

### Track day

Set the car, track, lane and driver once, note what you changed, and type or paste your lap times. A live preview shows best, typical and spread while you type. **Compare with last run** gives a plain verdict, such as "typical pace faster by 0.250 s", with a better/worse table and the setup differences, even before you save.

Saved runs carry a snapshot of the gearing, tyres, weight and RPM, and appear in Lap analysis, Progress, Compare runs and Records like any other lap session.

### Garage

**Library → Garage** holds your cars and tracks.

- Cars from Paddock on this computer arrive with each import: name, maker, class, technical configuration and photo.
- Add your own cars for anything that is not in Paddock, and tracks with their lanes and lane lengths.
- A car's page shows its setups and best lap per track and lane, with buttons to start a new setup or a Track day with it.

Setups can now name their car, and Track day suggests garage cars and tracks and uses the lane length you entered.

### Paddock on this computer

Connect to Paddock on the same computer with one click and no password. Every race in the collection is imported, including races Timing saved to a Shared library. Imports are incremental and verified, Telemetry reconnects when Paddock restarts, and corrections and withdrawals follow Paddock.

### Simpler to use

- The workbench opens on **Quick setup**: gearing, motor, rear tyres and weight. Switch to **Measure the car**, **Plan & test** or **Everything** when you need more. Hidden values are kept and still used.
- Analyze groups its modes into *Setups* and *Track laps*, and dims topics with nothing saved yet.
- **Settings → Units:** metric, imperial or your own mix. Saved files always stay metric.
- A **gear chart** shows rollout, speed or ratio for every pinion and driven gear; click a cell to try that gearing.
- Download a printable **setup sheet** for the workbench or any saved setup.

### Faster with a full library

With hundreds of setups, races and lap sessions, Telemetry starts in about half the time, opens Analyze and Library pages three to five times faster, and keeps up with your typing on the workbench and in race search. Your draft is still saved automatically, a moment after you stop typing and straight away when you close the app.

### Backups and updates

Telemetry now backs up all its data automatically: shortly after start-up, every 12 hours while open and when quitting, keeping the newest 10. You can also copy each backup to a folder of your choice, such as a USB stick or a cloud-synced folder. **Settings → Backups** lets you back up now, save a backup elsewhere and restore one. Every backup is checked before it replaces anything, and your current data is saved first.

Telemetry also tells you when a new version is out. A notice offers **Download**, which opens the release page, or **Not now**. Nothing is downloaded or installed automatically, and **Settings → Updates** lets you check manually or turn the check off.

### Review and compatibility

Local validation passed 244 automated tests, 3 Paddock interoperability tests, all 21 desktop suites and Windows packaging; four environment-dependent tests were skipped locally.

Existing setups and lap data remain readable. On first start, the setup library moves from window storage to plain files in Telemetry's profile folder; the old copy is left in place. Older versions ignore a setup's car.

### Choose your download

| Computer | File in Assets |
| --- | --- |
| Windows, 64-bit Intel/AMD | **SlotForgeTelemetry-0.14.0-windows-x64-Setup.exe** — installs with Start menu and desktop shortcuts. Or **…-Portable.exe** to run without installing. |
| Apple Silicon or Intel Mac | **SlotForgeTelemetry-0.14.0-mac-universal.dmg** — open and drag into Applications. The ZIP contains the same app. |
| Ubuntu / Debian / Mint, x64 | **SlotForgeTelemetry-0.14.0-linux-amd64.deb** — open with your software installer. |
| Other Linux desktops, x64 | **SlotForgeTelemetry-0.14.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage** — allow execution in Properties, then open. |

GitHub's **Source code** archives are for developers. **SHA256SUMS.txt** contains checksums for the downloads.

### Updating

Close Telemetry and replace the old application with the new download, or run the installer. Existing local data is retained. From this version on, Telemetry makes backups for you; export one from an older version first if you want to be safe.

See the [installation instructions](https://github.com/theDutchmanJames/SlotForgeTelemetry#how-to-install) for platform-specific help. Windows and macOS builds are not publisher-signed/notarized; the README explains the operating-system prompts.

Livery.body:
**SlotForge Livery 1.5.0 — The new look**

**A calmer look, rebuilt screens and stock cars to paint straight away**

## What's new

- **New look:** Graphite colours, new type and calmer buttons throughout Livery, with Light/Dark in the top right.
- **Paint Studio and Garage:** a Workbench layout, and one Garage page for cars, liveries, the library, the Trash and backups.
- **Showroom:** nine stock cars to paint when you don't have a drawing of your own.
- **Entries:** one livery on many cars, each with its own number and name.
- **Colours and printing:** livery colours with real paints and a shopping list, and a Print pack saved as one PDF.
- **Safer and faster:** exports and backups survive a crash, and the inspector and Print pack are much quicker.

## Everything in this release

**Look**
- A full restyle: Graphite colours, Barlow and Roboto Mono, flat buttons, quieter selections, and redesigned dialogs, Settings, Help and the welcome screen.
- The Light/Dark switch is back in the top right corner.

**Screens rebuilt**
- **Paint Studio:** Workbench layout with Layers on the left, view tabs, Selection and Workshop tabs, a quick bar and a right-click menu.
- **Garage:** one page for cars, liveries, the library, the Trash and backups.
- **Car setup:** a guided, step-by-step preparation of a new car.
- **Colours:** livery colours with real paints, the paints you own and a shopping list.
- **Print pack:** pick and order the pages, then save them as one PDF.
- **Side by side:** edit two sides together, mirrored or the same.
- **Help on the spot:** help for the screen you are on (F1), tours and a keyboard sheet.
- **Start page:** a proper welcome when you open Livery.
- **Arrivals:** imported packages arrive in the Garage, where you can check them or send them back.
- **Rescue window:** if the library cannot be read, Livery finds your backups and brings one back.

**New**
- **Entries:** one livery, many cars, each with its own number and name.
- **Showroom:** nine stock cars ready to paint.
- **Update window:** replaces the daily update check, shows what's new and downloads the update for you.

**Speed**
- The inspector is about five times faster; the Print pack draws about eight times faster.
- Side by side, Panel Studio and exports are quicker.

**Fixes**
- Exports and backups no longer damage an earlier file if Livery stops while writing; an interrupted restore leaves nothing behind.
- Typing a name and then clicking other artwork no longer renames the wrong piece.
- Liveries saved by older versions get their Garage summary rebuilt, so the Garage can group them.
- Two library items with the same id can no longer be merged silently.
- Opening a file that is not a Livery package gives a plain message.
- Many smaller fixes from a full review.

## Downloads

Every system has both an **installer** and a **portable app**:

- **Windows:** `…-windows-x64-setup.exe` (installer) or `…-windows-x64-portable.exe`.
- **macOS**, when supplied: `.dmg` (installer) or `.zip` (portable), for Intel (`x64`) and Apple silicon (`arm64`).
- **Linux:** `.deb` (installer) or `.AppImage` (portable), for x64 and arm64.

Both open the same library on a computer, so you can switch between them. EPS/PDF conversion is bundled and works offline. No account is required. Windows applications are unsigned; macOS packages are not notarised.

## Updating

Your existing library stays in the same location and opens as before. Designs that use the new features, such as Entries, may not show fully in older versions.

## Verification and source

Release assets are published only after their native build and packaged checks pass. This release also adds random-save, crash, random-click and coverage tests.

Livery is licensed under **GNU AGPL version 3 or later**. Corresponding source archives, build instructions and checksums accompany the downloads.

Decals.body:
# SlotForge Decals 0.3.0

Print & cut for cutting machines and hand cutting, a Windows installer, faster everyday editing and a tidier workshop.

## Print & cut

- A new **Print & cut** panel sets how decals are cut out: lines that **follow each decal's shape** or a **rectangle**, with an offset around the artwork (default 1 mm). Nearby parts such as letters share one cut line and holes are not cut. Dashed lines on the sheet show the result, and any decal can override the sheet setting.
- **Export for cutter…** saves a folder with step-by-step instructions for **Silhouette Studio** (including the free Basic edition), **Cricut Design Space** or **Brother ScanNCut**. Each decal becomes a 300 DPI PNG with a white border along its cut line: inkjets print white as no ink, while the cutter software traces the border. Sheet files keep the exact layout: a page PNG with DXF cut lines for Silhouette, or an SVG with print and cut layers. The cutter software adds its own registration marks.
- **Print cut lines in the PDF** adds thin lines for cutting by hand or scanning a printed sheet with a ScanNCut.
- These files are checked for size and structure but have not yet been tested on every machine. Print on plain paper first.

## More ways to create

- **Batch racing numbers:** fill in *More numbers* (for example 1-30, 44, 51) in Racing Number Plates to create a plate or matching pair for every car at once; they fill free space and add pages as needed.
- **Recolour…** lists every colour in the selected decals, including inside SVG artwork, named colours and default black, and replaces the ones you change: handy for team variants.
- **Add mirrored copy (other side)** flips directional graphics such as arrows and stripes for the other side of the car. Editable text stays readable; lettering inside imported logos is mirrored too.
- **US Letter** and **custom paper sizes** (50–600 mm) join A4, A5 and Photo 4×6 in.
- **Four new cars** in the car preview: classic endurance GT, touring saloon, rally hatchback and Group C prototype, each with side and top views. Choosing a car sizes the model from the real car's length at your scale.

## Everyday editing

- **Copy, cut and paste** decals with Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V, also between sheets. Paste a copied image, a screenshot or SVG code to import it.
- **Choose installed font…** lists every font on your computer with a preview and embeds the chosen one in the sheet, so PDFs and shared sheets keep it.
- Every colour field has an **eyedropper** and quick **swatches** of your recent colours and the colours on the sheet.
- New artwork is placed in **free space** on the page instead of on top of existing decals.
- **Opacity** is a percentage slider with a live preview, and **undo** keeps 200 steps.

## A tidier workshop

- The **car preview** stays pinned at the top of the right panel while you edit a decal.
- **Import & Export** and the library windows follow the dark and light theme.
- Toolbar buttons that need a selection are greyed out with a hint until they can be used.
- **Help** is split into searchable topics with a keyboard-shortcut table.
- The PDF review lists one row per decal, merges identical copies and names any bitmap parts.
- The older .sfbackup format moved into a collapsible section of Settings.

## Faster with big workspaces

- Decals starts in about half the time, and saving no longer slows down as the workspace grows: on a test workspace with 2,000 decals and 300 sheets, autosave went from about 1 second to 60 ms.
- Saved sheets open faster, and the Sheet Library shows its previews almost instantly.
- Dragging, box-selecting and zooming stay smooth on busy pages with many logos and cut lines.

## Update notice

- About 15 seconds after starting, Decals asks GitHub whether a newer version has been published, at most twice a day. Only the version number is requested; nothing about you or your sheets is sent.
- A newer version shows a notice above the sheet bar: **Download** opens the release page in your browser, **Not now** hides it until an even newer version appears. Decals never downloads or installs anything by itself.
- **App Settings → Updates** shows the result, has **Check now** and turns automatic checks off.

## Updating and installing

Your saved sheets and decals remain in **Documents/SlotForge Decals**, outside the application. Sheets that use US Letter, a custom size or cut-line settings need Decals 0.3.0 or newer. Back up first through **Settings → Backup & Recovery → Export Complete Backup**.

| Computer | Installer | Portable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows x64 | windows-x64-setup.exe | windows-x64-portable.exe |
| Intel Mac | mac-x64.dmg | mac-x64.zip |
| Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or newer) | mac-arm64.dmg — drag Decals to Applications; ZIP also available |
| Linux x64 | linux-amd64.deb | linux-x86_64.AppImage |
| Linux ARM64 | linux-arm64.deb | linux-arm64.AppImage |

The Windows installer installs for your user account only, lets you choose the folder and never deletes your workspace when uninstalling. Apple Silicon downloads are added after their separate build passes. Mac builds require macOS 15 or newer. Windows builds are unsigned; Smart App Control may block them. Mac builds are ad-hoc signed, not Apple-notarized. Updates are never installed automatically.

## Verification and sources

Local verification passed **143 unit tests** and **29 desktop suites**, including new checks for print & cut packages (DPI, millimetre sizes, DXF and SVG), copy and paste, clipboard images, installed fonts, recolouring, mirrored copies, batch numbers, custom paper and the update notice. The packaged Windows build passed the packaged acceptance suites. All test workspaces are isolated from user data.

Licensed under **AGPL-3.0-or-later**; application source, corresponding Ghostscript and MuPDF sources, revision records and build instructions accompany the release. Bundled components retain their notices in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt.

Foundry.body:
The first public release of SlotForge Foundry: design slot-car track, plan a layout and 3D print every part, with a full STL editor built in.

## What's new

- **Track Set:** design a piece's road, cross-section, borders, markings, joints and print segments, with every change shown live before you apply it.
- **Track Planner:** snap pieces into a layout, add bridges with support blocks, see it in 3D and export the full print kit with a parts list.
- **Special pieces:** add a hairpin, diamond crossing, pit lane, duel, chicane or timing straight to any pack with one click.
- **STL Edit:** create parts from scratch, or edit, repair and combine any STL model.
- **Library:** keep your packs, layouts and STL parts on your computer, with backup and restore.
- **Desktop app:** an installer and a portable app for Windows, macOS and Linux, with the SlotForge themes and an update check.

## Getting started

Start with one of the two starter packs, **SlotForge Basic** (two lanes, 200 mm road) or **SlotForge Basic Single Lane** (100 mm). Or make your own pack, or import a layout from **SlotForge Circuit** (SVG or DXF). Before printing a whole track, print the **fit samples** from Home to find the clip clearance that suits your printer and filament.

The [README](https://github.com/theDutchmanJames/SlotForgeFoundry/blob/v1.0.0/README.md) gives a short tour, and the [user guide](https://github.com/theDutchmanJames/SlotForgeFoundry/blob/v1.0.0/docs/GUIDE.md) explains every tool.

## Verification

602 unit tests passed on Windows, covering the track geometry, connectors, drawing imports, the Library, the update check and where the data is kept. 60 browser stages clicked through the shipped app with networking disabled. The desktop app was started twice on a portable data folder to check that saved data survives a restart. Its update window was tested against a simulated GitHub release, including a download checked against its checksum.

Robustness tests ran random sequences of Library saves and compared both storage paths. They interrupted the app during saves, autosave, restore and the Planner cache, and made thousands of random clicks through the interface.

The macOS and Linux downloads are built and tested by GitHub Actions after this release is published, on each operating system.

## Install

| System | Installer | Portable app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | `SlotForgeFoundry-1.0.0-Setup-x64.exe` | `SlotForgeFoundry-1.0.0-Portable-x64.exe` |
| macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) | `SlotForgeFoundry-1.0.0-mac-universal.dmg` | `SlotForgeFoundry-1.0.0-mac-universal.zip` |
| Linux (x64) | `SlotForgeFoundry-1.0.0-linux-amd64.deb` | `SlotForgeFoundry-1.0.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux (ARM) | `SlotForgeFoundry-1.0.0-linux-arm64.deb` | `SlotForgeFoundry-1.0.0-linux-arm64.AppImage` |
| Any browser | `SlotForge-Foundry-1.0.0.zip`: extract it and open **SlotForge Foundry.html** | |

Foundry is not code-signed. On Windows, choose **More info → Run anyway**. On macOS, use **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway** the first time. On Linux, mark the AppImage as executable (`chmod +x`). The SHA256SUMS files list each download's checksum.

The portable app and the AppImage keep everything in a **SlotForge Foundry Data** folder beside the program. The installed app uses its user-data folder. The desktop and browser editions keep separate Libraries; use **Library → Backup & restore** to move your work between them.
